chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said:

When Ādam عليه السلام died and it came time to perform the prayer over him, Hibatullāh said to Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام, “Go forward, O Messenger of Allah, and perform prayer over the Prophet of Allah.” Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام said, “Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded us to prostrate to your father, so we do not go before the righteous among his offspring, and you are among the most righteous of them.” So he went forward and pronounced five takbīrs over him, equal to the number of prayers that Allah the Exalted made obligatory upon the Ummah of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and this is the ongoing sunnah among his offspring until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام, the angel addressed in the narration
key_terms.خَمْسًا: five takbīrs pronounced in the funeral prayer
key_terms.هِبَةُ ٱللَّهِ: Hibatullāh, the son of Ādam عليه السلام mentioned in the report
key_terms.يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection, marking the lasting scope of this practice
key_terms.ٱلسُّجُودِ: the prostration commanded to the angels before Ādam عليه السلام
key_terms.ٱلسُّنَّةُ ٱلْجَارِيَةُ: the continuing established sunnah among his offspring
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةِ: the funeral prayer performed over the deceased

ai.seo_question: Why are five takbīrs said in the funeral prayer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the funeral prayer of Ādam عليه السلام and presents Hibatullāh as the one who led it after Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام declined to precede the righteous offspring of Ādam عليه السلام. It also gives a basis for the five takbīrs in the funeral prayer and describes this as an enduring sunnah in his progeny until the Day of Resurrection.
